Thought: Looking at the IR spectrum, I can see a strong absorption band at 1738 cm⁻¹, which is characteristic of a C=O (carbonyl) group, typically found in esters or aldehydes. I can also see some other peaks in the carbonyl region (around 1611-1566 cm⁻¹) but these are more likely due to C=C aromatic stretches rather than carbonyls based on their frequencies.

Since I can clearly identify one strong carbonyl absorption at 1738 cm⁻¹, and no other peaks in the typical carbonyl region (1670-1820 cm⁻¹), I can conclude that the molecule contains exactly one C=O group.
Final Answer: 1
